Born in what is now Syria, this Roman emperor reigned from 244 to 249 during an unusually stable stretch of a turbulent century, after being proclaimed ruler when his predecessor died in battle — who is he?
Philip the Arab: Roman emperor from 244 to 249. Philip I (Latin: Marcus Julius Philippus; c. 204 – September 249), commonly known as Philip the Arab, was Roman emperor from 244 to 249.
Crowned king of a Rajasthan realm as a child in 1177, this ruler beat a Ghurid army near Taraori in 1191 - only to be defeated and executed there the following year. Who was he?
Prithviraj Chauhan: King of Ajmer from 1177 to 1192.

After her young son died and her husband the raja passed, she took up the leadership of her princely state and fought battle after battle against the British in the Indian Rebellion of 1857. Who is she?
Rani of Jhansi: Prominent leader of the 1857 Indian rebellion.
A U.S. attorney general turned New York senator, this icon of American liberalism was assassinated in 1968 — and his brothers John and Ted were no strangers to office either. Who is he?
Robert F. Kennedy: American politician and lawyer (1925–1968)
A career diplomat turned politician, this BJP member rose from foreign secretary to become India's longest-serving minister to hold the External Affairs portfolio exclusively. Who is he?
S. Jaishankar: Indian diplomat and politician (born 1955)

Taking his regnal name — which meant "the legitimate king" — from an ancient ruler of Akkad, this Neo-Assyrian monarch founded a new dynastic line and aspired to conquer the known world before dying in battle in 705 BC. Who was he?
Sargon II: King of the Neo-Assyrian Empire. Over the course of his seventeen-year reign, Sargon substantially expanded Assyrian territory and enacted important political and military reforms.
Born in 1940, she is the eldest child of the last Shah of Iran and his first wife, Fawzia of Egypt — who is she?

It began as a Cold War quarrel over how to read Marx — Mao branding Moscow's de-Stalinization and 'peaceful coexistence' as revisionism — and slowly froze relations between two communist giants. What is this rift called?
Names of the days of the week
Racial segregation in the United States
Sino-Soviet split: Conflict between communist blocs.
A former professor turned politician, this leader has served in India's upper house of parliament since 2019 and acts as a senior national spokesperson for the Bharatiya Janata Party — who is he?
Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
A Princeton and Harvard Law graduate who became the first Hispanic American to represent the Lone Star State in the Senate, he led the charge in the 2013 government shutdown — who is he?
Ted Cruz: American politician and attorney (born 1970)

Blaming rich families' land-grabbing for a supposed decline in Rome's population, this politician pushed an agrarian reform law to shift land to poorer citizens — and was killed for it in 133 BC. Who was he?
Tiberius Gracchus: Roman politician and social reformer (163 – 133 BC)

Emerging in Brazil during the 1920s, this monotheistic religion blends Spiritism, Afro-Brazilian Candomblé, and Roman Catholicism, with spirits called orixás beneath a distant God — what is it called?
Umbanda: Afro-Brazilian syncretic religion. Umbanda (Portuguese pronunciation: [ũˈbɐ̃dɐ]) is a religion that emerged in Brazil during the 1920s.
Also called Narayana and Hari, this Hindu deity known as 'The Preserver' forms one third of the Trimurti alongside Brahma and Shiva — who is he?
This Luftwaffe ace was the first pilot in history to down 100 enemy aircraft and devised the famous finger-four formation — yet he died as a passenger in a plane crash. Who was he?
Werner Mölders: German World War II flying ace.
Elected tsar of Russia by the Seven Boyars in 1610 — though he never took that throne — this eldest son of Sigismund III went on to rule Poland and Lithuania; who is he?
Władysław IV Vasa: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1632 to 1648.
This third-century queen of the Palmyrene Empire conquered Egypt and expanded her realm across the Roman East before facing Emperor Aurelian's counterattack — who is she?
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Maria Mitchell is an astronomer. Maria Mitchell ( mə-RY-ə; August 1, 1818 – June 28, 1889) was an American astronomer, librarian, naturalist, and educator.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Barium?
Barium: Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
What is the atomic number of Nickel?
Nickel: Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
In what year was Zhuge Liang born?
Zhuge Liang: After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
In what year was John McAfee born?
John McAfee: In 1987, he wrote the first commercial anti-virus software, founding McAfee Associates to sell his creation.
In what year was Max Planck born?
Max Planck: Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck (German: [ˈmaks ˈplaŋk]; 23 April 1858 – 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
In what year did Vikram Sarabhai die?
Vikram Sarabhai: Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
In what year did Michael Faraday die?
Michael Faraday: Although Faraday received little formal education, as a self-made man, he was one of the most influential scientists in history.
In what year was Lithium discovered?
Lithium: Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Which country is Dassault Falcon 900 from?
Dassault Falcon 900: France. The Dassault Falcon 900, commonly abbreviated as the F900, is a French-built corporate trijet aircraft made by Dassault Aviation.
Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this economist ran the Federal Reserve for its second-longest tenure ever — who is he?
Alan Greenspan (born March 6, 1926) is an American economist who served as the 13th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006.
Before sharing the 2010 Nobel for graphene, this Manchester physicist won an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog using its own magnetism — who is he?
Andre Geim (born 21 October 1958) is a Russian-born British physicist working in England in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester.
This red giant is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes and the fourth-brightest star in the entire night sky — name the star?
Arcturus is a red giant star in the northern constellation of Botes, and the brightest star in the constellation.
This American physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for decisive contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish (born January 27, 1936) is an American experimental physicist and Nobel Laureate.
So dense that not even light can escape its gravity, this astronomical object's boundary of no return is called the event horizon — name it?
Black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
Also called meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the carrot family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — name it?
Caraway (Carum carvi), also known as meridian fennel, is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae, native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa.
Her famous experiment proved that parity is not conserved — yet the 1957 Nobel went to two male colleagues while she earned the first-ever Wolf Prize in Physics. Which Manhattan Project physicist?

Chien-Shiung Wu (pinyin: W Jinxing; May 31, 1912 - February 16, 1997) was a Chinese-American particle and experimental physicist who made significant contributions in the fields of nuclear and particle physics.

Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this genus of flowering shrubs and small trees in the Rubiaceae family produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and ground into a beloved beverage worldwide — which genus?
Coffea is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The seeds of some species, called coffee beans, are roasted and ground to brew into various coffee beverages.
Affecting roughly 1 in 22,000 births and more common in girls, which genetic condition caused by a chromosome 5 deletion takes its French name from a feline-sounding cry?
Cri du chat syndrome is a rare genetic disorder due to a partial chromosome deletion on chromosome 5.
With interlocking neck vertebrae that prevent almost any head movement, which genus of prehensile-tailed marsupials is commonly called the large American opossums?
Didelphis is a genus of New World marsupials.
This English physician created the world's first vaccine, targeting smallpox, and in doing so coined the very term 'vaccine' — derived from the Latin for 'pustules of the cow.' Who was he?
Edward Jenner (17 May 1749 - 26 January 1823) was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines and created the smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
This class of mental health condition is defined by an enduring, pervasive pattern of behavior, emotion, and thought that deviates from social norms and develops early in life. What is it?
Erythritol is an organic compound, the naturally occurring achiral meso four-carbon sugar alcohol (or polyol).
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Bred for centuries to hunt by sight and speed rather than scent, this ancient dog breed's deep chest, flexible spine, and long legs make it one of the fastest breeds alive. Name the breed?
Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.
This discipline governs the design and formal description ('blazon') of coats of arms, crests, and other armorial bearings — what is it called?
Heraldry (also known as armoury) is a discipline relating to the design, display, study and transmission of armorial bearings.

This altered mental state involves intensely focused attention, reduced awareness of surroundings, and heightened responsiveness to suggestion, though scientists still debate whether it's truly a distinct state of consciousness — what is it?

Hypnosis is a human condition involving focused attention (the selective attention/selective inattention hypothesis, SASI), reduced peripheral awareness, and an enhanced capacity to respond to suggestion.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.
Born in Los Angeles to South Korean immigrant parents, this NASA astronaut and physician previously served as a Navy SEAL on over 100 combat missions — who is he?
Jonny Kim (born 5 February 1984) is an American NASA astronaut, physician, U.S.
These paired folds of skin are the major externally visible structures of the vulva, with an outer 'majora' set and an inner 'minora' set — what are they called?
Labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva. In other mammals, the labia majora are not present and the labia minora are instead referred to as the labia vulvae.
Serving as a somatosensory organ as well as a tool for eating and forming sounds, this pair of soft facial features is one of the most visible parts of the mouth — what are they?
Lip are a horizontal pair of soft appendages attached to the jaws and are the most visible part of the mouth of many animals, including humans.
Roughly 60% the diameter of Pluto and stained reddish-brown by tholins, this trans-Neptunian dwarf planet carries minor-planet number 136472 — what is it?
Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
This natural biological transition marks the permanent end of menstrual periods, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as estrogen levels decline — what is it?
Menopause is the time when menstrual periods permanently stop, marking the end of the reproductive stage for the female human.
With over 86,000 living species spanning sea, freshwater, and even land, this is the largest of all marine phyla — what is it?
Mollusca is a phylum of protostomic invertebrate animals, whose members are known as molluscs or mollusks.

The first recognized fossil of this archaic human group was unearthed in 1856 in a German valley, and the species vanished around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived; who were these Pleistocene Europeans?

Neanderthal (nee-(r)-TAHL, nay-, -THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene.
Despite counting the killer whale and pilot whale among its roughly forty species, this marine mammal family is more closely related to porpoises than to true whales — what family is it?
Oceanic dolphin are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.

Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's used in classroom and lab experiments, this single-celled ciliate thrives in freshwater, brackish, and marine habitats — what organism is it?
Paramecium ((ee-)m, -see-m, plural "paramecia" only when used as a vernacular name) is a genus of eukaryotic, unicellular ciliates, widespread in freshwater, brackish, and marine environments.
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.
This inflammation of the lining around the lungs causes sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing, and is most often triggered by a viral infection — what condition is it?
Pleurisy is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Along with his two brothers, this American physician-turned-businessman acquired the pharmaceutical company behind OxyContin, later linked to the U.S. opioid crisis — who is he?
Raymond Sackler (February 16, 1920 - July 17, 2017) was an American physician and businessman.

Named after the naturalist who first documented it, this highly venomous South Asian snake is known for an extremely painful bite and ranks among the region's 'Big Four' dangerous species — what snake is it?
Russell's viper (Daboia russelii) is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
Made by Novo Nordisk and taken by injection or pill, this peptide medicine doubles as a diabetes treatment and a weight-management drug — what is it?
Semaglutide is an anti-diabetic medication used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, and an anti-obesity medication used for weight management.
This alkaline compound, commonly diluted in water and sold as household bleach, is derived from hypochlorous acid and is unstable in its pure anhydrous form. What is it?
Sodium hypochlorite is an alkaline inorganic chemical compound with the formula NaOCl (also written as NaClO).

This eye disorder causes the eyes to misalign when looking at an object; if it develops in childhood it often leads to a 'lazy eye,' while adult onset usually causes double vision instead — what condition is it?
Strabismus is an eye disorder in which the eyes do not properly align with each other when looking at an object.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.
Dolphins, porpoises, beaked whales and sperm whales all belong to this cetacean group that diverged from baleen whales around 34 million years ago — what's the collective name?

Toothed whale (also called odontocetes, systematic name Odontoceti) are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth, such as beaked whales and the sperm whales.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.

This genus of four woody, twining vine species in the legume family is native across East Asia and parts of North America, and became a popular ornamental after being introduced to Europe — what genus is it?
Wisteria is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family, Fabaceae (Leguminosae).
Also known by his Latinized name Rhazes, this Persian polymath authored over 200 manuscripts on medicine, philosophy, and astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age — who was he?
Abu Bakr al-Razi: 10th-century Iranian physician and polymath.
Based on a civilian widebody jet, this European aerial-refueling tanker holds over 90% of the air-to-air refueling market outside the United States, with 17 countries as customers — which aircraft?

Airbus A330 MRTT: Aerial refuelling tanker aircraft. The Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) is a European aerial refueling and military transport aircraft based on the civilian Airbus A330.
About one-third the density of steel, this soft, nonmagnetic, silver-looking metal grows a protective oxide skin the instant it meets air — which element, symbol Al?
Aluminium: Chemical element with atomic number 13 (Al)
Its name comes from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest,' and it describes pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle — what is this condition called?
Angina: Chest discomfort due to disorder of the heart muscles.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
Found from the Labrador Sea to the Barents Sea and able to live up to 25 years, this widely eaten fish can occasionally top 180 centimeters and 50 kilograms — what species is it?
Atlantic cod: Species of fish. The Atlantic cod (pl.: cod; Gadus morhua) is a fish of the family Gadidae, widely consumed by humans.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?
Buried penis: Male congenital condition. A buried penis can lead to urinary difficulties, poor hygiene, infection, and inhibition of normal sexual function.
Its Latin name means 'horned goat,' and it's often pictured as a half-goat, half-fish sea creature — which is the smallest constellation of the zodiac?
Capricornus: Zodiac constellation in the southern hemisphere.

Nicknamed the 'solar' web for its sunburst of radiating nerve fibers, this abdominal structure sits behind the stomach and in front of the diaphragm's crura, near where several major arteries branch off the aorta — what is it?
Celiac plexus: Complex network of nerves located in the upper abdomen.
Discovered entirely by accident and marketed as Librium, this 1960-approved medication was the first benzodiazepine ever synthesized — what is it?
Chlordiazepoxide: Benzodiazepine medication. Chlordiazepoxide hydrochloride, sold under the brand name Librium, is a sedative and hypnotic medication of the benzodiazepine class.
This little Indo-Pacific reef fish, banded in white, shelters among stinging tentacles and repays the favor by fending off anemone-eaters and fanning its host clean. What fish is it?
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
The second jet fighter to enter RAF service and the first powered by a single jet engine, this twin-boom aircraft flew with the Halford Goblin turbojet — which aircraft?

De Havilland Vampire: Fighter aircraft; first single-engine jet in RAF service. The de Havilland DH100 Vampire is a British jet fighter developed and manufactured by the de Havilland Aircraft Company.

Previously known as multiple personality condition and popularized (inaccurately) by the case of 'Sybil,' this controversial mental health diagnosis is characterized by the presence of two or more distinct personality states known as 'alters' — which condition is this?
Dissociative identity disorder: Mental illness with multiple personality states.
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
Also known as the Indian bison, this Vulnerable-listed bovine is the largest living member of the wild cattle family, with most of its roughly 21,000 individuals found in India — what animal is it?
Gaur: Largest species of the bovid family.

A colorless, sweet-tasting, syrupy liquid, this sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of triglycerides in fats and oils, and doubles as a food-industry sweetener. What is it?

Once nearly all lumped into a single genus before 21st-century research proved that grouping polyphyletic, these grey-and-white seabirds have an older dialect name, 'mew,' echoing their calls — which birds?
Gull: Subfamily of seabirds. The large species take up to four years to attain full adult plumage, but two years is typical for small gulls.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
First published as a Latin anagram in 1676 by a British physicist, this principle states that the force needed to stretch a spring scales linearly with its extension — which law?
Hooke's law: Force needed to pull a spring grows linearly with distance.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
Traditionally kept as an indoor watchdog, this small non-sporting dog breed hails from Tibet — which breed?
Lhasa Apso: Tibetan breed of dog. The Lhasa Apso ( LAH-sə AP-soh) is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Sold under the brand name Cozaar, this angiotensin receptor blocker treats high blood pressure while also protecting the kidneys in diabetic patients — what drug is it?
Losartan: Blood pressure medication. Losartan, sold under the brand name Cozaar among others, is a medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
In 2013, this tech billionaire took his own computer company private in a $24.4 billion buyout, the largest since the Great Recession, before it went public again in 2018 — who is he?
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.
A Jesuit priest and polymath from the Republic of Ragusa produced an early precursor of atomic theory and, in 1753, discovered that the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich: Croat-Italian physicist and writer (1711–1787)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
